sourcePriority: Use NCERT performance instructions and do/dont guidance over conflicting archive images. Routine memberships come from the user, not efficacy claims from this catalog.

interpretation.idealMeaning: A textbook-aligned geometric reference for the selected variant; not a clinically validated healthy range of motion or a safety threshold.
interpretation.degreesNullMeaning: The source describes this position qualitatively and does not justify a single numeric ideal. Null is not zero; do not score it or silently substitute a number.
interpretation.geometricTranslationMeaning: A numeric consequence of idealized straight/perpendicular/parallel segments. Not a number explicitly printed in NCERT, and not a demand to force end-range joints.
interpretation.bothSidesMeaning: Whether the selected pose variant is performed once per left/right side, one after the other. This does not describe camera views or calibration sides.
interpretation.roles: For asymmetric poses resolve raised/supporting/resting and upper/lower roles from the currently practiced side. Never duplicate an active-leg angle onto the supporting leg.
interpretation.measurement: Interior joint angles are 0-180 degrees and use aspect-corrected 2D coordinates in the indicated plane. They differ from clinical flexion/extension angles. Front and side views are not interchangeable.
interpretation.futureScoring: No personal targets, tolerances or calibration are defined here. Some metrics improve by increasing (extension); others by decreasing (interior hip angle during a leg raise). Non-angular relations are also needed.
interpretation.unmeasurable: Standard Pose Landmarker joints do not directly measure spinal curvature, cervical ROM, pain, breathing, relaxation, muscle engagement, toe grip or palm contact.

shoulder.meaning: 0: upper arm along torso toward hip; 180: upper arm extending away from hip along torso axis.

elbow.meaning: 180: straight elbow; lower values: more bend.

hip.meaning: 180: aligned torso/thigh; 90: perpendicular torso/thigh. Shoulder-to-hip is a trunk proxy, not the anatomical pelvic axis.

knee.meaning: 180: straight knee; lower values: more bend.

ankle.meaning: Shin-to-forefoot proxy; not clinical ankle ROM.

legElevationFromFloor.meaning: 0: straight leg along floor; 90: vertical leg. Use hip-to-ankle with a straight-knee check and an established floor direction; not knee angle.

torsoElevationFromFloor.meaning: 0: trunk along floor; 90: upright trunk. Use a visible same-side torso proxy only when both sides cannot be tracked; not a spinal angle.

torsoTiltFromVertical.meaning: 0: upright trunk; greater values: increasing lean. Lateral bend requires front view and a separate forward/backward lean check.

armSeparation.meaning: Angle between left shoulder-to-elbow and right shoulder-to-elbow vectors; 180: opposite directions; 90: perpendicular directions.

neckExtension.meaning: Clinical cervical extension is not available directly from standard pose landmarks. No numerical target is inferred.

poses.name: Tadasana
poses.variant: NCERT palm-tree posture: overhead parallel arms, raised heels

sideRequirement.rationale: Both arms stretch and both heels rise together; no separate left/right repetition.

shoulder.rationale: Upper arms are aligned with the upright torso, beside the ears.

hip.rationale: Erect body with no forward or backward bend.

torsoTilt.rationale: Head, neck and body stay vertically aligned.

ankle.rationale: Heel elevation is required, but the book sets no plantar-flexion angle; lift height depends on comfortable capacity.

postureRules: Keep feet together, arms parallel overhead and palms facing each other.
Raise both heels and balance on the toes without bending the torso.
Lower the heels before lowering the arms.
notes: This catalog follows NCERT. The existing app uses the earlier palms-together, heels-grounded image variant and is not changed.
180-degree alignment is a geometric reference, not an instruction to force or lock a joint.

poses.name: Vrikshasana
poses.variant: Overhead prayer, with one foot against the opposite inner thigh

sideRequirement.rationale: After right-leg placement and release, step 5 explicitly repeats using the left leg.

shoulder.rationale: Overhead-arm variation extends both arms upward.

elbow.rationale: Straight overhead arms in the supplied reference.

raisedHip.rationale: The raised thigh opens outward; the book does not give an abduction or flexion degree.

raisedKnee.rationale: Bend sufficiently to place the sole high on the opposite inner thigh. Foot height and body proportions change this angle.

torsoTilt.rationale: The final posture should not bend the body.

postureRules: Place the sole of the lifted foot against the inside of the opposite thigh, with heel up and toes down.
Keep the torso upright, join palms overhead, and look at a fixed point.
Release and repeat with the other leg.
notes: The textbook also allows prayer hands at the chest. Its arm angles differ from the overhead variant.
The elbow alignment for overhead prayer is inferred from the reference variant, not an explicit degree in the text.

shoulder.rationale: Hands joined at the chest; no fixed shoulder angle is specified.

elbow.rationale: Elbows bend to join palms at the chest; no exact angle is specified.

alternativeVariants.postureRule: Join palms in front of the chest instead of overhead; leg and torso rules remain the same.

poses.name: Vajrasana
poses.variant: Kneeling seat, buttocks supported by heels

sideRequirement.rationale: Legs are folded one at a time to enter a single bilateral seated posture. Entry order is not separate left/right practice.

hip.rationale: An erect torso above approximately horizontal thighs gives a right angle in the idealized side-view geometry.

knee.rationale: Knees are deeply folded, but thigh/calf contact and proportions determine the interior angle; the book supplies no degree.

shoulder.rationale: Hands rest on the knees; exact shoulder placement depends on arm and thigh length.

elbow.rationale: Hands rest on the knees; neither a fixed elbow degree nor locked elbows is required.

ankle.rationale: Feet sit beneath the buttocks with heels outside and toes arranged as described; no ankle angle is specified.

torsoTilt.rationale: Spine erect without forward or backward bend.

postureRules: Fold both legs beneath you and rest the buttocks on/between the heels as described in the textbook.
Keep the hands on the respective knees and the spine upright.
Arrange heels outside and big toes overlapping; gaze forward or close the eyes.
notes: The 90-degree hip value is idealized segment geometry; it is not a clinical hip-flexion measurement.

poses.name: Makarasana
poses.variant: Prone relaxation, head resting on crossed arms

sideRequirement.rationale: Both arms form a cushion and both legs relax together; no side-specific repetition.

knee.rationale: Legs extend while resting on the floor; keep the limbs relaxed rather than forcing extension.

hip.rationale: Legs are spread at a comfortable distance. A frontal hip angle changes with that spread; the text fixes no angle.

shoulder.rationale: Hands hold opposite shoulders to form a cushion; the precise shoulder angle is not specified.

elbow.rationale: Elbows are folded and stacked, or slightly separated if necessary; no exact elbow degree is given.

torsoElevation.rationale: Rest prone on the floor rather than lift into a cobra.

postureRules: Rest prone with legs comfortably apart, heels inward and toes outward.
Fold the arms so the hands hold opposite shoulders; rest the head on this cushion.
Allow slightly separated elbows if stacking is difficult; avoid pressure that makes breathing uncomfortable.
notes: The supplied image shows a head-on-forearms relaxation variant. The catalog records the textbook crossed-arm instructions.
Angles cannot establish relaxation or comfortable breathing.

poses.name: Shavasana

sideRequirement.rationale: Whole-body supine relaxation is performed once, not as left/right repetitions.

elbow.rationale: Rest arms extended beside the body; this is a nominal relaxed alignment, not a demand for tension.

knee.rationale: Rest legs extended on the floor without tension.

hip.rationale: Legs are comfortably apart. The hip angle depends on spread and viewpoint; the book provides no fixed degree.

shoulder.rationale: Hands rest about six inches away from the body; this distance does not imply a universal shoulder angle.

torsoElevation.rationale: Back and trunk rest on the floor.

postureRules: Lie on the back with legs comfortably apart and arms a little away from the body.
Turn palms upward, allow fingers to relax, and keep the head centered.
Relax the body and attend to natural breathing.
notes: 180-degree limb values represent nominal extended geometry; relaxed slight bending should not become an error merely because it differs from an exact line.
Palms, eye closure, breathing and relaxation require additional checks beyond joint angles.

poses.name: Ardhashalabhasana

sideRequirement.rationale: Raise and lower the right leg, then repeat with the left leg.

knee.rationale: Do not bend either knee while lifting a leg.

elbow.rationale: Arms remain extended along the body.

shoulder.rationale: Upper arms extend alongside the torso.

restingHip.rationale: Resting leg extends in line with the prone torso.

raisedHip.rationale: Lift to comfortable capacity only while the pelvis remains untilted. No fixed hip-extension angle is supplied.

raisedLegElevation.rationale: The book explicitly limits elevation by pelvic stability, not by a universal degree.

torsoElevation.rationale: Keep the trunk down and chin resting on the floor.

postureRules: Raise only one straight leg at a time and keep the other leg on the floor.
Stop the lift before the pelvis tilts; keep the chin down.
Lower slowly, then repeat on the other side.
notes: A hip interior angle alone cannot distinguish extension from flexion; prone orientation and upward leg direction must also be checked.

poses.name: Ardhahalasana

sideRequirement.rationale: Both legs lift together through the stages to the final vertical hold.

legElevation.rationale: Final leg elevation is explicitly 90 degrees.

hip.rationale: With the torso on the floor and thighs vertical, the shoulder-hip-knee interior angle is 180 - 90 = 90 degrees.

knee.rationale: Legs must remain straight throughout raising and lowering.

elbow.rationale: Arms extend along the sides with palms on the floor.

torsoElevation.rationale: Keep the trunk supported by the floor.

postureRules: Keep legs together and straight, hands beside the body and palms on the floor.
Raise through 30, 45 and 60 degrees to the 90-degree final hold.
Lower slowly through the same stages without jerks.
notes: The 30/45/60-degree values describe movement stages, not interchangeable final ideals.

poses.name: Niralamba Bhujangasana
poses.variant: NCERT forearm-supported cobra with chin resting in palms

sideRequirement.rationale: Both arms support the chest and chin together; there is no alternating side hold.

knee.rationale: Both legs extend together on the floor.

hip.rationale: Lift the head and chest up to the navel at comfortable capacity; no numeric back-extension angle is specified.

shoulder.rationale: Forearms support the raised chest while the hands support the chin. Exact shoulder angle is not specified.

elbow.rationale: Bend elbows and bring wrists together so the chin can rest in the open palms; no exact bend angle is stated.

torsoElevation.rationale: Chest lifts with forearm support, but no fixed degree of lift is given.

neckExtension.rationale: Head is raised/backward in the described posture, but no cervical angle is specified or measurable directly from standard pose landmarks.

postureRules: Lie prone with legs extended, heels and toes together.
Raise the head, neck, shoulders and chest with forearm support, keeping the lower body down.
Bend elbows, bring wrists together and rest the chin in the open palms.
Use comfortable capacity without force or jerking.
notes: The archive image shows a straight-arm, palms-on-floor cobra. It does not match this textbook Niralamba Bhujangasana variant; its elbow angles must not be used as this pose ideal.
Shoulder-hip-knee geometry is only a rough torso/leg relation, not a measurement of spinal or cervical extension.

poses.name: Trikonasana
poses.variant: Lateral bend with lower hand to foot and upper arm upward

sideRequirement.rationale: The textbook describes a left bend but does not explicitly instruct a right-side repeat in these steps. Separate mirrored practice is inferred for this asymmetric pose.

elbow.rationale: Arms extend down/up in the standard straight-arm variation.

knee.rationale: The text forbids knee bending during the side bend.

armSeparation.rationale: The text explicitly gives 180 degrees between the two extended arms in the standard final posture.

lowerShoulder.rationale: Shoulder angle depends on torso inclination as the lower hand reaches the foot.

upperShoulder.rationale: A 180-degree inter-arm angle does not fix the individual shoulder-to-torso angle.

hip.rationale: Foot spacing, lateral bend and body proportions change each hip angle; no numeric hip value is given.

torsoTilt.rationale: Bend laterally from the waist within capacity; the textbook does not specify a lateral-bend degree.

postureRules: Start with feet approximately 1-2 feet apart and arms extended at shoulder height.
Bend to one side from the waist, lower that hand to the same-side foot, and extend the other arm upward.
Keep knees straight and avoid leaning forward or backward.
Return upright; mirror the posture for the other side as the catalog convention.
notes: requiresBothSides=true is an implementation interpretation here, unlike the explicit alternation in Vrikshasana, Hastottanasana and Ardhashalabhasana.
Measure arm separation between the upper-arm direction vectors, not the shoulder-elbow-wrist elbow angle.

armSeparation.rationale: The textbook allows the upper arm to reach toward the bending side, making 90 degrees between the arms.

alternativeVariants.postureRule: Upper arm reaches toward the side of the bend; do not score this optional variant against the primary 180-degree arm separation.

poses.name: Hastottanasana
poses.variant: Overhead interlocked hands with alternating lateral bends

sideRequirement.rationale: After the right-side bend and return to center, step 5 explicitly asks for left-side practice.

elbow.rationale: The text explicitly requires straight arms.

knee.rationale: Standing legs stay extended during the waist bend.

shoulder.rationale: Keep upper arms extended overhead along the upper torso in the idealized alignment.

torsoTilt.rationale: Bend sideways from the waist as far as comfortably possible; the text specifies no lateral-bend degree.

hip.rationale: Lateral trunk bend changes projected hip angles; the textbook gives no fixed value.

postureRules: Stand with feet together; raise arms, interlock fingers and turn palms upward.
Bend from the waist to the right without bending forward or backward.
Return to center, then repeat the lateral bend to the left.
notes: The supplied illustration shows feet apart; the textbook starting position specifies feet together.
This is the textbook side-bending variation, not a generic overhead or backward stretch.

poses.name: Paschimottanasana
poses.variant: Seated forward fold with straight legs and slightly bent elbows

sideRequirement.rationale: Both legs stay together and the torso folds forward once; no separate left/right posture.

knee.rationale: Do not bend the knees while folding forward.

hip.rationale: Reach forward and try to bring the forehead toward the knees within comfort. Spinal curvature and proportions prevent a universal shoulder-hip-knee ideal.

shoulder.rationale: Arms reach to the toes with the head between them; exact shoulder angle is not stated.

elbow.rationale: The text deliberately calls for a little elbow bend, without quantifying it; 180 degrees must not be imposed.

torsoElevation.rationale: A forward fold is required, but neither floor-parallel torso nor a particular torso angle is specified.

postureRules: Sit with legs extended together and reach forward to hold the toes.
Keep knees straight, elbows slightly bent, and head between the arms.
Try to bring the forehead toward the knees without strain or jerks; hold only at a comfortable level.
notes: Forehead-to-knee and hand-to-toe proximity are useful relational checks; forcing a zero-degree hip angle would not be justified by these instructions.

poses.name: Uttanapadasana
poses.variant: Dvi-Pada: supine double-leg raise up to 60 degrees

sideRequirement.rationale: Primary variant lifts both legs simultaneously. The optional Ek-Pada variant requires separate left/right repetitions.

legElevation.rationale: The final elevation described by NCERT is up to 60 degrees, after 30- and 45-degree stages.

hip.rationale: With the trunk down, the interior hip angle is 180 - 60 = 120 degrees, not 60 degrees.

knee.rationale: Do not bend the knees during the raise.

elbow.rationale: Arms extend along the body, palms on the floor.

torsoElevation.rationale: Trunk and head remain on the floor.

postureRules: Lie on the back with legs together, arms beside the body and palms on the floor.
Raise both straight legs through 30 and 45 degrees to 60 degrees while keeping the trunk down.
Lower slowly through 45 and 30 degrees to the floor.
notes: The supplied image shows approximately vertical legs (90 degrees), which conflicts with the textbook endpoint. The catalog uses 60 degrees.
requiresBothSides applies to the chosen variant; do not reuse the false flag for single-leg practice.

sideRequirement.rationale: The text raises/lowers the left leg and explicitly repeats with the right leg.

legElevation.rationale: Single raised leg progresses up to 60 degrees.

hip.rationale: Raised-side interior hip angle is 180 - 60 = 120 degrees.

restingHip.rationale: The resting leg stays extended along the floor.

alternativeVariants.postureRule: Lift one straight leg while the other remains down, release, then repeat with the other leg.

poses.name: Naukasana
poses.variant: NCERT supine boat with straight legs

sideRequirement.rationale: The legs and trunk rise together; no separate side-specific repetition.

torsoElevation.rationale: The textbook explicitly raises the head/trunk up to 45 degrees.

legElevation.rationale: The wording groups legs with the simultaneous 45-degree trunk raise and asks that they not rise in an unparallel way. Equal 45-degree elevations are the chosen interpretation, not a separately stated leg angle.

hip.rationale: For trunk and legs each elevated 45 degrees on opposite sides of the hip, the interior angle is 180 - 45 - 45 = 90 degrees.

knee.rationale: The selected straight-leg supine boat variant uses extended legs, consistent with the supplied reference.

elbow.rationale: The text explicitly asks for straight arms without elbow bending.

shoulder.rationale: Stretch and raise arms; NCERT supplies no floor-relative arm direction, so an exact shoulder degree is not implied.

postureRules: Begin supine with feet together; lift the straight legs and head/trunk simultaneously.
Keep arms stretched without bending the elbows and hold comfortably.
Lower the head/trunk, then legs and arms slowly.
notes: The book mentions prone Naukasana but provides the supine instructions here; the catalog does not invent a prone variant.
The illustrative torso-to-floor target is a segment proxy, not a measurement of spinal curvature.
